title: Working Together When Nobody Agrees Completely

paragraphs.en: As a neighborhood garden expanded, volunteers disagreed about how to use the new space. Some wanted vegetables, whereas others preferred flowers. Neither option was obviously wrong, nor could the group satisfy everyone without compromise. The coordinator asked why each proposal mattered and whether its supporters could describe the needs behind it. This was not just a contest of taste. A resident needed affordable food because his income was low, while another wanted a quiet place for grieving. Their aims were different but could exist together, provided the discussion did not reduce people to opposing labels.
paragraphs.zh: 社区花园扩大时，志愿者对新空间用途有分歧：有人种菜，有人种花。两者都未明显错误，若无妥协也无法满足人人。协调人问建议为何重要，支持者能否说明背后需求。这不仅是品味竞赛：低收入者需要便宜食物，另一人想有安静地方悼念。目的不同，却能共存，只要不把人简化成对立标签。

paragraphs.en: According to the original rules, decisions required a simple majority. However, the coordinator believed that voting too quickly would obscure important information. She therefore invited people to speak in pairs instead of delivering speeches to the whole group. They discussed gardening versus recreation, plus the time needed for maintenance. The results were revealing: even committed flower growers also wanted useful crops, and vegetable supporters valued beauty. The group had somehow treated overlapping interests as incompatible positions. By listening carefully, volunteers could examine the assumptions whereby they had reached that mistaken conclusion and thereby find a more workable starting point.
paragraphs.zh: 根据原规则，简单多数即可决策。然而协调人认为太快投票会掩盖重要信息，因此请人两两交谈，替代全体演说。讨论种植与休憩，也加上维护时间。结果显示花卉支持者也要实用作物，种菜者也重美。小组不知怎地把重叠利益视为不相容。认真聆听让大家检查导致错误结论的假设，从而找到更可行起点。

paragraphs.en: Although cooperation sounded attractive, a plan still needed limits. Each household could receive one small plot, except those unable to provide regular care. Such residents could join a shared area instead. Moreover, the group reserved a path through the site so visitors could walk regardless of whether they owned a plot. Participation remained open irrespective of age or income. Lest the rules become vague, the coordinator wrote down the specific responsibility attached to every role. The question was not who deserved the garden most, but how a shared arrangement could remain fair when contributions differed.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管合作有吸引力，方案仍需界限。每户可有一小块地，不能定期照顾者除外，但可加入共有区。此外留贯穿小径，访客无论有无地块都能行走。参加不受年龄收入限制。为免规则模糊，协调人写明各角色具体责任。问题不是谁最配拥有花园，而是贡献不同如何仍公平。

paragraphs.en: A budget shortage threatened the agreement. Unless volunteers found cheaper materials, the design would fail; otherwise, they could begin before spring. Besides the costs of tools, there were insurance payments per year and expenses for water. Some members wanted to proceed anyway, though the coordinator advised caution. They could reduce the plan or seek donations, but neither solution was effortless. Notwithstanding these difficulties, a local builder offered recycled timber, and several residents supplied equipment. Others did likewise with plants. Accordingly, the team revised its spending estimate, hence removing the immediate obstacle without pretending that future maintenance would be free.
paragraphs.zh: 预算短缺威胁协议。除非找到便宜材料，否则方案失败；若找到，则春前可开工。除工具，还有每年保险与水费。有人无论如何想开动，协调人建议谨慎。可缩减或募捐，两者均不轻松。尽管困难，建筑商提供再生木材，居民送工具，别人同样捐植物。于是修改支出估算，消除眼前障碍，也不假装未来维护免费。

paragraphs.en: The garden opened with one unresolved issue, namely the hours when visitors could enter. Nonetheless, members agreed to review the schedule after a trial. There was little else to gain from arguing before observing actual use. The coordinator said that disagreement need not disappear for action to become possible. Volunteers could work anyhow, if they remained willing to revise a decision in light of experience. Thus the project became a modest lesson in public cooperation. Despite imperfect agreement, people could share responsibility; nevertheless, this required clear rules and patient conversation rather than a cheerful slogan about unity.
paragraphs.zh: 花园开放时还有一个问题，即开放时段，但成员同意试行后复核。未观察实际使用前再争论，几乎无其他收获。协调人说，分歧不必消失才可行动，只要愿据经验改决定，就能继续干。项目由此成为公共合作的小课：尽管共识不完美，人们仍可共担责任；然而需清楚规则与耐心对话，而非欢快团结口号。
